title: Genetic background sets the trajectory of cancer evolution
authors: Aitken SJ; Connor F; Feig C; Rayner TF; Lukk M; Luft J; Aitken S; Arnedo-Pac C; Hayes JF; Nicholson MD; Sundaram V; Verburg JC; Connelly J; Anderson CJ; Behm M; Campbell S; Daunesse M; Ewing A; Kaiser VB; Kentepozidou E; Pich O; Redmond AM; Santoyo-Lopez J; Sentís I; Talmane L; Flicek P; López-Bigas N; Semple CA; Taylor MS; Odom DT
one_liner_zh: 该文研究小鼠种系遗传背景对肿瘤进化轨迹的影响，聚焦体细胞突变与克隆选择，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作、转录因子结合或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Human cancers are heterogeneous. Their genomes evolve from genetically diverse germlines in complex and dynamic environments, including exposure to potential carcinogens. This heterogeneity of humans, our environmental exposures, and subsequent tumours makes it challenging to understand the extent to which cancer evolution is predictable. Addressing this limitation, we re-ran early tumour evolution hundreds of times in diverse, inbred mouse strains, capturing genetic variation comparable to and beyond that found in human populations. The sex, environment, and carcinogenic exposures were all controlled and tumours comprehensively profiled with whole genome and transcriptome sequencing. Within a strain, there was a high degree of consistency in the mutational landscape, a limited range of driver mutations, and all strains converged on the acquisition of a MAPK activating mutation with similar transcriptional disruption of that pathway. Despite these similarities in the phenotypic state of tumours, different strains took markedly divergent paths to reach that state. This included pronounced biases in the precise driver mutations, the strain specific occurrence of whole genome duplication, and differences in subclonal selection that reflected both cancer susceptibility and tumour growth rate. These results show that interactions between the germline genome and the environment are highly deterministic for the trajectory of tumour genome evolution, and even modest genetic divergence can substantially alter selection pressures during cancer development, influencing both cancer risk and the biology of the tumour that develops.
abstract_zh: 人类癌症具有异质性。其基因组在复杂且动态的环境中，从遗传多样性的种系进化而来，包括暴露于潜在致癌物。人类自身的这种异质性、我们的环境暴露以及随后的肿瘤，使得理解癌症进化在多大程度上是可预测的变得具有挑战性。为解决这一局限性，我们在多样化的近交系小鼠品系中重复运行了早期肿瘤进化数百次，捕获了与人类群体相当甚至超越其的遗传变异。性别、环境和致癌物暴露均受到控制，并通过全基因组和转录组测序对肿瘤进行了全面分析。在品系内部，突变景观具有高度一致性，驱动突变范围有限，且所有品系均趋同于获得MAPK激活突变，并伴有该通路相似的转录干扰。尽管肿瘤在表型状态上存在这些相似性，不同品系却采取了显著不同的路径达到该状态，包括精确驱动突变的明显偏向、全基因组重复的品系特异性发生，以及反映癌症易感性和肿瘤生长速率的亚克隆选择差异。这些结果表明，种系基因组与环境之间的相互作用对肿瘤基因组进化轨迹具有高度决定性，即使适度的遗传差异也能显著改变癌症发展过程中的选择压力，影响癌症风险和所形成肿瘤的生物学特性。
